If you're not already familiar with the holiday, here's a little background:

On June 19, 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas and delivered the news that enslaved people were free — more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation had already been signed. In 2021, Juneteenth was officially recognized as a federal holiday, a long-overdue acknowledgment of its place in American history.

 

We hope you'll take the day to rest, reflect, and learn something new about this important piece of our shared history. We are proud to honor this important day alongside our employees and the broader community.

New Math Academic Screener

  • Access research-backed assessments recommended by the National Center on Intensive Intervention (NCII)
